_provenance.note: LLM reading of the lens token tables; not a measurement

axes.label: percent/quantity units ↔ digit/arithmetic framing
axes.rationale: Real-logit correlation separates ' percent', ' per', ' pct', ' cents', ' mph' (negative) from ' digit', '-digit', ' multiplied', '-sided' (positive). The Jacobian lens agrees, with ' percent' and numeric fragments on the negative end and '-digit', ' ×', '→' on the positive end. Logit and tuned lenses only share '-digit'.

axes.label: counted nouns/plural entities ↔ arithmetic operation continuations
axes.rationale: Real-logit positive tokens are operations (' plus', ' minus', ' divided', ' multiplied', ' raised', ' followed'). Real-logit negative tokens are nouns a number would count (' stories', ' comments', ' states', ' people', ' teams'). The lenses are mostly noise, though ' CFR' and number fragments recur on the negative end.

axes.label: time/percent units (year, month) ↔ comparative/function-word continuations
axes.rationale: Real-logit negative tokens are '-year', ' year', ' oct', ' Percent', ' pct', and the Jacobian lens adds month names (' October', ' November', ' September'). Real-logit positive tokens are function words such as ' more', ' less', ' instead', ' or'. Jacobian positive tokens (backtick code fragments) and the logit/tuned lenses look like noise.
